title: Floral dip transformation of Arabidopsis
author: Meike Burow
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5j6g4re

steps.title: Electroporate Arabidopsis Cells
steps.instruction: Perform electroporation and recover transformed cells before plating and incubation.

substeps.instruction: Electroporate cells using 2400 V, 220 Ω, 25 µF in a 1 mm cuvette.
Recover cells for 3 h in 1 mL YEP medium placed in a 15 mL tube at 28 °C.
Plate the recovered cells on YEP agar containing the appropriate antibiotics.

steps.title: Prepare Agrobacterium Culture
steps.instruction: Grow a fresh Agrobacterium culture and plate a small aliquot for overnight growth.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate 5 mL YEP medium with antibiotics with Agrobacterium and grow overnight at 28 °C, 220 rpm.
Take 1–2 mL of the overnight culture and spread onto YEP agar plates containing the same antibiotics; allow the liquid to soak into the agar.
Incubate the plated culture overnight at 28 °C.

steps.title: Floral Dip Transformation
steps.instruction: Prepare dip solution, immerse plants, and finish with drying before transfer to growth chamber.

substeps.instruction: Scrape cells from the YEP plates and resuspend them in 50 mL solution containing 10 mM MgCl₂·6H₂O (2.03 g/L), 5 % sucrose (50 g/L), and 0.005 % Silwet L‑77 (50 µL/L).
Transfer the suspension into a small bag.
Place each Arabidopsis pot upside‑down into the bag, gently massage so that unopened buds are slightly cracked.
Cut a small hole in the bag corner and pour the agro‑solution into the next bag for the following plant.
Leave the plants in the bags overnight in the dark to suppress immune response.
Remove the bags, allow the plants to air‑dry, then move them to the growth chamber.
